```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 3.8, eval = TRUE)
library(poissonCloud)
```

## 1. The Poisson baseline

If requests arrive independently at a steady rate, the number per window is Poisson.

```{r base}
overload_probability(40, 55)      # risk of exceeding 55 requests per window
required_capacity(40, 0.999)      # capacity for a 99.9% SLA
```

## 2. Where Poisson breaks

```{r data}
d <- load_traffic()
train <- which(d$day <= 7)
m <- fit_traffic_model(d$requests[train], d$timestamp[train])
m   # seasonal NB model: note the Pearson dispersion >> 1
```

After removing daily seasonality, the variance is still about 12 times the mean. Poisson's tail is far too thin:

```{r coverage}
te <- which(d$day >= 11 & d$is_incident == 0)
c(poisson = mean(d$requests[te] <= traffic_quantile(as_poisson(m), d$timestamp[te], 0.999)),
  negbin  = mean(d$requests[te] <= traffic_quantile(m, d$timestamp[te], 0.999)))
```

## 3. Burst model

```{r hawkes}
ev <- simulate_hawkes(mu = 5, alpha = 0.6, beta = 1, horizon = 300, seed = 1)
fit_hawkes(ev, 300)$branching_ratio
```

## 4. Digital twin and policy comparison

```{r twin, eval = FALSE}
valid <- which(d$day >= 8 & d$day <= 10); test <- which(d$day >= 11)
res <- compare_policies(d$requests, d$timestamp, m, train, valid, test)
res$test
```

## 5. Dashboard and API

`run_app()` starts the Shiny dashboard; `run_api()` exposes `/risk` and `/capacity` as JSON.
